da-false-claim.evidence: Full read of the proof at fb924525 (balanced case, Scope, the new affine-case classification with its three cases, Classical limit, (a,a+1) family, Open directions). Case 3 (b = -1), last step: 'Then D = qP + 1 obeys (1+q)D' = [3]_q D, forcing qP = -1'. False. With S = qP the all-odd step is (1+q)S' = [3]_q S + q; for D = S + 1 this gives (1+q)D' = [3]_q S + 1 + 2q, which differs from [3]_q D = [3]_q S + 1 + q + q^2 by q^2 - q. The correct shift is D = P + q^{-2} as in case 1 (equivalently q^2 P + 1 = X*s + 1 with s = qP, which is what the Lean affine_zero call uses), forcing P = -q^{-2}, which contradicts b = -1. Conclusion of the case is still true (and Lean-verified), but the displayed derivation step is wrong.
da-false-claim.notes: Fix: replace 'D = qP + 1' by 'D = q^2 P + 1' and 'forcing qP = -1' by 'forcing P = -q^{-2}, which has b = -2'.

da-false-claim.evidence: Full re-read of the proof at 028690e2 after the case b=-1 fix (balanced case, Scope, affine-case classification cases 1-3, Classical limit, (a,a+1) family, Open directions). Case 3 all-odd step now reads 'D = P + q^{-2} obeys (1+q)D' = [3]_q D as in case 1, forcing P = -q^{-2}, which has ord_q = -2 != -1'. Checked: (1+q)(P'+q^-2) = [3]_q P + 1 + q^-2 + q^-1 = [3]_q (P + q^-2); iterating around a k-cycle gives ((1+q)^k - [3]_q^k) D = 0, so D = 0, contradicting b = -1. The earlier major finding (D = qP + 1, qP = -1) is resolved. Cases 1 and 2 and the balanced case re-checked: no false step found.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: [first real review 2026-11-21; no hashed entry existed] I checked the proof by hand. The odd step P -> ([3]P+1)/[2] and the even step P -> P/[2] compose to A P + B with A = [3]^k_odd / [2]^k. With A = 1 the cycle condition forces B = 0, but B is a nonempty sum of positive terms when k_odd >= 1, so B > 0 at every real q > 0 and B is nonzero in Q(q). Coprimality: [3] - q[2] = 1, so [3] is congruent to 1 mod [2], and [2] = 1+q is not a unit in Z[q] or Z[q^+-1]; hence [3]^a = [2]^k has no solution with a, k >= 1 there. The plastic-number example also checks: rho^3 = rho + 1 gives [2] = rho^3 and [3] = rho^5, so [3]^3 = [2]^5 = rho^15. The proof matches the re-scoped statement (balanced-holonomy case only), and the Scope paragraph correctly leaves the A != 1 case open. Minor: 'b_i = 1/[2]_q^{.}' has a stray exponent placeholder; on an odd step b_i = 1/[2]_q.
